R11 (CLOSED 2026-11-25): the durable-run use cases had no HTTP surface; closed by NEX-009-HTTP (VERIFIED on e817d04). The same class of gap in the audit trail - a trail written but unreadable - was closed by NEX-011 (VERIFIED on f50a78d) and hardened against tampering by NEX-012 (VERIFIED on 3aade7c).

R12 (low, process): writing prose or scripts through a shell heredoc corrupts them in this environment. Write scripts and messages to files with file_editor and execute the file. It recurred this run and aborted a STATE.md update before it wrote anything.

R13 (low): PlannedStep.capability is derived from the tool catalog, so a plan cannot understate its authority. Any future plan construction path must go through PlannedStep or it reintroduces the gap; the derived field is what enforces it, not the use case.

R14 (new, low): the tool-invocation trail stores only arguments_digest, so an auditor can prove a call happened but cannot reconstruct its payload. That is deliberate (the trail must not become a second copy of note content), but a future investigation may want an explicit, separately-authorized payload-retrieval path rather than widening this one.

R15 (new, low): the audit chain seals each invocation over its predecessor, but the chain head is not anchored outside the database. An attacker who can rewrite the whole table can produce a self-consistent chain. Anchoring the head hash externally is the next hardening step, not a regression.

R15 (low, open): the audit chain head is not anchored outside the database, so an attacker able to rewrite the whole table could forge a self-consistent chain. External anchoring of the head hash is the next hardening step for NEX-012.

R16 (new, low): an approval's expires_at is nullable and is_usable treats NULL as 'never expires'. Needed only for rows written by an older app version during a rolling deploy; the backfill populates every pre-existing row. Tighten to NOT NULL once no old writer can exist.

R17 (new, low, process): a data-backfill migration tested only against an empty database is untested and will stay green while it crashes on the first real row. NEX-013 shipped exactly that - 'requested_at + timedelta' raised TypeError on SQLite's string value, aborting the upgrade and leaving expires_at NULL (i.e. unbounded). Any migration that reads existing rows needs a test that seeds a row at the previous revision; see tests/persistence/test_migrations.py::TestApprovalValidityBackfill.
